1. Verdict in brief

  • Layout is sound: 17 turns, built lap 4287.7 m vs real 4.304 km (−0.4 %), 1.24 km main straight vs real ≈1.2 km, no surface folds, verify-track and audit-circuit pass on the merged tree.
  • The weak points are dressing and atmosphere, not geometry: generic neon-capable city towers crowd the pit straight and the T3 → Horquilla leg (the brief says park first), overcast/fog do not change the sky, and a few authored strips and slabs read as floating.
  • Lighting merge #1979 applied cleanly. Wet, rain and storm at day now look daytime-dark (not night); dusk and night lamps fire.

6. Ranked defects

Each is tied to code. Suggestions are not applied. Rendered evidence is from the frames above; mechanisms marked GUESS were not traced to the engine.

1. Tall generic city towers on the pit straight and T3 → Horquilla leg (visible, high)

MEASURED day-dry 01 and 03: red/ochre brick towers 15–30 m off the road at lap frac 0.0 and 0.33, in the brief's "park before city" zones. At night the same towers carry neon pink/cyan bands (night-dry 01, 03) although night:false and Mexico is a daytime circuit.

SOURCE js/circuits/mexico.js:35,39: the generic city pass is excluded only for 0.02–0.30 and 0.48–0.94. The gaps are 0.94 → 0.02 (the whole pit straight) and 0.30 → 0.48. cityStyle (:89-92) still lists neon colours and neon kinds, which is why night shows neon.

Suggested fix: extend the exclusion to {kind:"city", s0:0.94, s1:1.0}, {s0:0, s1:0.02} and {s0:0.30, s1:0.48} (the authored cityFront at :330-345 already supplies the skyline there), and drop the neon kinds or set bias lower. Re-run verify-track and the terrain-over-road spec, since tests pin prop counts.

2. Overcast and fog barely change the sky (wrong weather response)

MEASURED day-overcast frames are visually identical to day-dry: same saturated blue sky and sun-lit ground. Day-fog only adds a pale haze at distance; the sky above stays deep blue. Wet, rain and storm do respond (grey sky, dark ground, reflective road).

GUESS mechanism: the day branch of js/lighting/atmosphere.js:236-252 derives ovc from _bias, and the cloud deck _cloudBase = 0.44 + ovc*0.42; the overcast/fog enum may not feed _bias. Not traced; this is shared engine code (just modified by #1979), not Mexico data. Check on another circuit before blaming Mexico.

3. Papel-picado banner strips render as long diagonal chords (visible, medium)

MEASURED day-dry 02 (left of the straight, pink-green strip slanting into the grass) and 06 (infield of the Foro Sol corner, strip crossing the lawn).

SOURCE scenery/mexico.js:46-52 banners() places five 6 m boxes on consecutive nodes at one lateral gap; on a curve the chord leaves the verge. The Foro calls :668 (banners(s,±1,9)) sit 9 m off a 15–24 m radius corner.

Suggested fix: orient each box on its own node tangent or skip when onTrack/terrain slope differs, and raise gap on tight bends.

4. Flat lawn / field slabs read as floating green rectangles (visible, medium)

MEASURED day-dry 06 and trackside 06: a hard-edged flat green slab hovering over the sloping ochre infield; edges show against terrain.

SOURCE :446-509 groundPatch (foro-infield-*, 28×28 m, 0.6 m thick) and the lawn/plaza table at :486-492 (0.4 m slabs). Flat boxes sit on terrain that falls away around them.

Suggested fix: raise samples, skirt the slab edges below grade or use per-sample drape, and tint closer to the terrain colour.

5. Orbit and trackside cameras sit inside the main stand roof at lap 0 (tooling)

MEASURED every weather, frame 01: a grey slab fills the left of frame; trackside 01 is a dark wall. The stand's roof is at 11.4 m (mexico.js scenery :178-181) on the left, 16 m off the road.

GUESS the camera back-off steps round buildings it knows about, not modelGroup roofs. Retake at --side -1 or --through if a clean S/F frame is wanted.

6. Foro Sol night: bowl and floodlight masts stay dark

MEASURED night-dry 06 and night-rain 06: stands read as faint white steps, no light spill, masts at 0.74–0.85 do not visibly cast. Roadside lamps work.

SOURCE lightMast() (:54-80) emits geometry only; the lighting is engine-side and authored for night:true circuits. Low priority since Mexico is a day race.

7. Brief is stale on banking and on landmark fractions (docs)

SOURCE docs/tracks/mexico.md §3 says the banking is "6° at s≈0.97 easing to 5°" and §5 puts the Peraltada at 0.90–0.97. MEASURED: max bank 5.99° at 0.693 (T11) and 3.5° at 0.892–0.930; there is no bank after 0.93. The brief also puts Horquilla at 0.42 (built 0.45–0.51) and the stadium at 0.72–0.88 (built bowl 0.728–0.858, turns 0.826–0.882).

Suggested fix: update the brief, or move bankZones if the real Peraltada bank (turn 17, "slightly banked", Wikipedia) is meant to be at the end of the lap.

7. Code and scenery deep-dive

How the file is organised

  • Helpers first (:18-143): cityBand, PIT=1, STAND=-1 (paddock on the right, main stand on the left, mirrored on purpose, :19-26), palette, banners, lightMast (emissive head and ground pad sampled from terrainYAt so it cannot bury), lampPost, avenue (jacaranda 50 %, plane 34 %, huizache 16 %, skipping SOLID arcs listed :104-116), kerb.
  • Main straight (:146-278): 8 bounded stands, gantry, scoreboard mast and screen at 50 m, lamps, 4 white paddock suites with flag-colour fascia, motorhomes, control tower, hospitality tents, 4 fascia runs.
  • Park belt (:279-345): hedges, forestEdge + avenue on both sides, brick pavilions, 3 cityFronts and 3 towers. Skyline band every 96 nodes at 460–550 m (:360-376).
  • Midlap (:377-509): Horquilla grandstand, kerbs, sports pavilions, Palacio de los Deportes, statue, plazas and lawns.
  • Foro Sol (:511-720): entry/exit portals, bowl via tieredBowl and terrace with sealed backs, scoreboard, crowd speckles, hoardings, fence and wall, 5+ floodlight masts.
  • Peraltada (:721-790), perimeter fences (:795-801), billboards (:803-808), named stands (:818-831), horizon ring + volcanoes (:940-985), airliner (:987-1057).

Cross-checks

  • Real facts: 17 turns and 4.304 km match; Foro Sol baseball stadium replaces the old Peraltada inner section (Wikipedia). The two volcano bearings come from the real coordinates in the file comment (131.1°/117.9°), compressed 35×; GUESS they read right in frames (mountains look like generic grey pyramids, snowcaps faint).
  • Brief vs source: the brief's lucha-libre statue exists as 4 boxes at 0.66 (:439-446), not a detailed figure; "thin-air haze" is only the palette's fogDensity 0.0022, and the day frames show a saturated sky, not a washed one.
  • Frac frame: no sceneryStartFrac, so none of the frac-keyed tables need the _sceneryShift compensation; the in-file comment (mexico.js:8-17) records that a former 0.635 shift put the paddock on the wrong straight.
  • Dead / odd code: the cityBand() helper (:18) only chooses tree distance; every(24) and every(22) tree loops skip s<0.50 despite the comment saying park sections are "handled elsewhere", so 0.14–0.50 depends on forestEdge and avenue alone.

8. Not captured / uncertain

  • Cut from the planned matrix: nothing in the ~6-position × weather set was dropped. Not taken: eye and trackside for the non-dry weathers, dusk/night overcast, fog and storm, and dawn. Orbit only for weather; no aerial/map view (survey-track.mjs not run).
  • Frames are TLX on SwiftShader (no real GPU): lighting and bloom may differ on a player's GPU. llvmpipe and WGX/GLX were not used.
  • Defect 2 mechanism, the mountains' look, and the Foro Sol night lighting are not traced to engine code (GUESS).
  • Real-world checks used one source (Wikipedia). Elevation profile, camber and width were compared to nothing external; path.len is OSM-derived and was not re-validated. Clockwise direction is from memory.
  • graph-parity and a driven lap (physics, kerbs, banking feel) not run; no browser test group was run (read-only survey).
